newsitem.title: CHINA: Beijing-anointed legislature meets in HK.
newsitem.headline: Beijing-anointed legislature meets in HK.

text.p: Hong Kong's Beijing-anointed provisional legislature began its first formal session in the former British colony on Tuesday shortly after the handover to China.

The 60-member assembly met to pass an omnibus law activating a string of legislation, including curbs on protests and the funding of political parties, which had been approved before the formal handover at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday.
The nine-part bill will also endorse the appointments of top judges of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) and the establishment of its legal system.

"In the next few months we will make every effort to enact the electoral law for the first Legislative Council of the Hong Kong SAR so that an election...can proceed as soon as possible," Rita Fan, the chamber's president, told the legislators.
The territory's new leader Tung Chee-hwa has pledged the elections will be held next May.
The provisional legislature took over from a Legislative Council partially elected under democratic reforms introduced by Britain.
